title: Soft drink, cola, fruit or vanilla flavored

content.title: About
content.content: A soft drink with cola, fruit or vanilla flavor is a non‑alcoholic beverage made by carbonating water and adding sugar (or sweeteners), flavorings, acid (usually phosphoric), and sometimes caffeine. The cola version has a characteristic caramel taste, the fruit version offers bright berry or tropical notes, and the vanilla version provides a smooth sweet vanilla nuance.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial carbonated drink was sold in England in 1767.
Cola drinks are named after the kola nut, originally used as a caffeine source.
Fruit sodas often use fruit concentrates, but most flavors are synthetically produced.
Vanilla‑flavored soda appeared in the 1970s as an alternative to traditional cola.
Carbonation enhances the perception of freshness and sweetness.

items.title: Hydration
items.content: The water base helps maintain the body’s fluid balance.

items.title: Quick Energy
items.content: Sugar (or its substitutes) provides a rapid rise in blood glucose, giving a short‑term energy boost.

items.title: Stimulation
items.content: Caffeine, present in many versions, can improve alertness and reduce fatigue.

items.title: Vitamin Content
items.content: Some fruit‑flavored variants are fortified with vitamin C and other antioxidants.

items.title: Flavor Enhancement
items.content: Carbonation stimulates taste buds, making the drink taste brighter.

items.title: High Sugar Content
items.content: Regular consumption can contribute to weight gain, tooth decay, and increased risk of metabolic diseases.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Phosphoric and citric acids may irritate the stomach lining and erode tooth enamel.

items.title: Caffeine
items.content: Excess intake can cause insomnia, anxiety, and rapid heartbeat.

items.title: Artificial Sweeteners
items.content: They may cause gastrointestinal discomfort in some individuals.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: Certain flavorings can trigger allergic reactions in sensitive people.

content.title: How to Consume
content.content: Soft drinks are typically served chilled in a glass or bottle. They can be used in cocktails, mixed drinks, and culinary applications such as marinades, glazes, and desserts.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 3–5 days to retain carbonation.
